  "output_head": "# Dual-read / Active Storage-write support for User and Organization profile pictures.
#
# New profile pictures are stored in Active Storage via `has_one_attached :profile_image`.
# Existing records with a legacy CarrierWave filename in the `profile_image` column continue
# to resolve via `ProfileImageUploader` until a new picture is uploaded or records are migrated.
module ProfileImageable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[
    image/jpeg
    image/gif
    image/png
    image/x-icon
    image/vnd.microsoft.icon
    image/bmp
    image/x-ms-bmp
    image/webp
    image/x-adobe-dng
    image/tiff
  ].freeze
  MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION = 4096

  included do
    has_one_attached :profile_image

    before_save :record_profile_image_attachment_change
    before_save :clear_legacy_profile_image_if_cleared
    before_save :strip_profile_image_exif
    after_commit :cleanup_profile_image_tempfiles
    after_rollback :cleanup_profile_image_tempfiles

    validate :validate_profile_image
  end

  attr_reader :remote_profile_image_url

  def profile_image=(attachable)
    @remote_profile_image_url = nil
    @profile_image_download_error = nil

    if attachable.nil? || attachable == ""
      @profile_image_cleared = true
      super(nil)
    elsif attachable.is_a?(String)
      if (blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(attachable))
        @profile_image_cleared = false
        super(blob)
      else
        # Preserve CarrierWave behavior when non-file strings (e.g. URL strings)
        # are passed directly to `profile_image=`.
        self
      end
    else
      @profile_image_cleared = false
      super(attachable)
    end
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url=(url)
    @remote_profile_image_url = nil
    @profile_image_download_error = nil

    return if url.blank?

    unless url.is_a?(String)
      self.profile_image = url
      return
    end

    @remote_profile_image_url = url
    download_and_attach_remote_profile_image(url)
  end

  def profile_image_url
    if profile_image.attached?
      active_storage_profile_image_url
    elsif legacy_profile_image_present?
      legacy_profile_image_url
    end
  end

  def serializable_hash(options = nil)
    super.tap do |hash|
      hash["profile_image"] = { "url" => profile_image_url } if hash.key?("profile_image")
    end
  end

  def legacy_profile_image_present?
    legacy_profile_image_identifier.present?
  end

  private

  def legacy_profile_image_identifier
    return unless has_attribute?(:profile_image)

    self[:profile_image]
  end

  def legacy_profile_image_for_validation?
    return false if @profile_image_cleared

    legacy_profile_image_present?
  end

  def legacy_profile_image_url
    identifier = legacy_profile_image_identifier
    return if identifier.blank?

    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(self, :profile_image)
    uploader.retrieve_from_store!(identifier)
    uploader.url
  end

  def active_storage_profile_image_url
    attachment = profile_image.attachment
    return unless attachment

    if attachment.blob&.persisted?
      format_active_storage_url(
        Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_blob_path(profile_image, only_path: true),
      )
    elsif persisted? && profile_image_attachment&.persisted?
      format_active_storage_url(
        Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_blob_path(profile_image_attachment, only_path: true),
      )
    elsif persisted? && legacy_profile_image_present?
      legacy_profile_image_url
    elsif attachment.blob
      format_active_storage_url(
        "/rails/active_storage/blobs/#{attachment.blob.key}/#{attachment.blob.filename}",
      )
    end
  end

  def format_active_storage_url(path)
    return path unless Rails.env.production? && URL.domain.present?

    URL.url(path)
  end

  def record_profile_image_attachment_change
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = attachment_changes["profile_image"].present?
  end

  def clear_legacy_profile_image_if_cleared
    return unless @profile_image_cleared && has_attribute?(:profile_image)

    self[:profile_image] = nil
  end

  def profile_image_changed?
    (has_attribute?(:profile_image) && saved_change_to_attribute?(:profile_image)) ||
      @profile_image_attachment_changed == true
  end

  def download_and_attach_remote_profile_image(url)
    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(self, :profile_image)
    remote_file = CarrierWave::Downloader::Base.new(uploader).download(url)
    return if remote_file.file.size.to_i.zero?

      filename: filename,
      content_type: remote_file.content_type

        record_id: record.id,
        name: "profile_image",

    def upload_blob(file, uploader, filename:, content_type:)
      if file.is_a?(CarrierWave::SanitizedFile) && file.path.present? && File.exist?(file.path)
        File.open(file.path, "rb") do |io|
          ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
            io: io,
            filename: filename,
            content_type: content_type,
            identify: true,
          )
        end
      else
        bytes = uploader.read
        return if bytes.blank?

        ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
          io: StringIO.new(bytes.b),
          filename: filename,
          content_type: content_type,
          identify: true,
        )
      end
    end

    def attach_and_refresh_caches(record, blob)
      ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
        record.lock!
        raise AlreadyAttachedError if attachment_exists?(record)

        ActiveStorage::Attachment.create!(
          name: "profile_image",
          record: record,
          blob: blob,
        )
        refresh_cached_articles!(record)
      end
    end

    def refresh_cached_articles!(record)
      record.association(:profile_image_attachment).reset
      cached_entity = Articles::CachedEntity.from_object(record)

      case record
      when User
        Article.where(user_id: record.id).update_all(cached_user: cached_entity)
      when Organization
        Article.where(organization_id: record.id).update_all(cached_organization: cached_entity)
      end
    end

    def purge_orphan_blob(blob)
      return unless blob&.persisted?
      return if ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(blob_id: blob.id)

      blob.purge
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn("profile_images:copy failed to purge orphan blob #{blob&.id}: #{e.message}")
    end
  end

    return if file.content_type.include?("svg")

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "module Images
  # Copies existing CarrierWave profile images for Users and Organizations into Active Storage.
  #
  # Designed to be safe to re-run if interrupted: records that already have an Active Storage
  # `profile_image` attachment are skipped, and each record's attachment and cached article
  # metadata are updated atomically.
  class CopyProfileImagesToActiveStorage
    BATCH_SIZE = 100
    MODELS = [User, Organization].freeze

    Result = Struct.new(:copied, :skipped, :failed, keyword_init: true)

    class AlreadyAttachedError < StandardError; end
    private_constant :AlreadyAttachedError

    def self.call(...)
      new(...).call
    end

    def initialize(models: MODELS, batch_size: BATCH_SIZE)
      @models = models
      @batch_size = batch_size
    end

    def call
      counts = { copied: 0, skipped: 0, failed: 0 }

      @models.each do |model_class|
        pending_scope(model_class).find_each(batch_size: @batch_size) do |record|
          outcome = copy_record(record)
          counts[outcome] += 1
        end
      end

      Result.new(**counts)
    end

    private

    def pending_scope(model_class)
      model_class
        .where.not(profile_image: [nil, ""])
        .where.missing(:profile_image_attachment)
    end

    def copy_record(record)
      identifier = record.read_attribute(:profile_image)
      return :skipped if identifier.blank? || attachment_exists?(record)

      uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(record, :profile_image)
      uploader.retrieve_from_store!(identifier)
      file = uploader.file

      if file.nil? || !file.exists? || file.size.to_i <= 0
        Rails.logger.warn(
          "profile_images:copy skipped #{record.class.name}##{record.id}: " \
          "missing or empty CarrierWave file (#{identifier})",
        )
        return :skipped
      end

      filename = File.basename(identifier.to_s).presence || "profile_image"
      content_type = file.content_type.presence
      blob = upload_blob(file, uploader, filename: filename, content_type: content_type)
      return :skipped unless blob

      attach_and_refresh_caches(record, blob)
      :copied
    rescue AlreadyAttachedError, ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      purge_orphan_blob(blob)
      :skipped
    rescue StandardError => e
      purge_orphan_blob(blob)
      Rails.logger.error(
        "profile_images:copy failed for #{record.class.name}##{record.id}: #{e.class}: #{e.message}",
      )
      :failed
    end

    def attachment_exists?(record)
      ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(
        record_type: record.class.name,
        record_id: record.id,
        name: "profile_image",
      )
    end

    def upload_blob(file, uploader, filename:, content_type:)
      if file.is_a?(CarrierWave::SanitizedFile) && file.path.present? && File.exist?(file.path)
        File.open(file.path, "rb") do |io|
          ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
            io: io,
            filename: filename,
            content_type: content_type,
            identify: true,
          )
        end
      else
        bytes = uploader.read
        return if bytes.blank?

        ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
          io: StringIO.new(bytes.b),
          filename: filename,
          content_type: content_type,
          identify: true,
        )
      end
    end

    def attach_and_refresh_caches(record, blob)
      ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
        record.lock!
        raise AlreadyAttachedError if attachment_exists?(record)

        ActiveStorage::Attachment.create!(
          name: "profile_image",
          record: record,
          blob: blob,
        )
        refresh_cached_articles!(record)
      end
    end

    def refresh_cached_articles!(record)
      record.association(:profile_image_attachment).reset
      cached_entity = Articles::CachedEntity.from_object(record)

      case record
      when User
        Article.where(user_id: record.id).update_all(cached_user: cached_entity)
      when Organization
        Article.where(organization_id: record.id).update_all(cached_organization: cached_entity)
      end
    end

    def purge_orphan_blob(blob)
      return unless blob&.persisted?
      return if ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(blob_id: blob.id)

      blob.purge
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn("profile_images:copy failed to purge orphan blob #{blob&.id}: #{e.message}")
    end
  end
end

module Images
  # Copies existing CarrierWave profile images for Users and Organizations into Active Storage.
  #
  # Designed to be safe to re-run if interrupted: records that already have an Active Storage
  # `profile_image` attachment are skipped, and each record's attachment and cached article
  # metadata are updated atomically.
  class CopyProfileImagesToActiveStorage
    BATCH_SIZE = 100
    MODELS = [User, Organization].freeze

    Result = Struct.new(:copied, :skipped, :failed, keyword_init: true)

    class AlreadyAttachedError < StandardError; end
    private_constant :AlreadyAttachedError

    def self.call(...)
      new(...).call
    end

    def initialize(models: MODELS, batch_size: BATCH_SIZE)
      @models = models
      @batch_size = batch_size
    end

    def call
      counts = { copied: 0, skipped: 0, failed: 0 }

      @models.each do |model_class|
        pending_scope(model_class).find_each(batch_size: @batch_size) do |record|
          outcome = copy_record(record)
          counts[outcome] += 1
        end
      end

      Result.new(**counts)
    end

    private

    def pending_scope(model_class)
      model_class
        .where.not(profile_image: [nil, ""])
        .where.missing(:profile_image_attachment)
    end

    def copy_record(record)
      identifier = record.read_attribute(:profile_image)
      return :skipped if identifier.blank? || attachment_exists?(record)

      uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(record, :profile_image)
      uploader.retrieve_from_store!(identifier)
      file = uploader.file

      if file.nil? || !file.exists? || file.size.to_i <= 0
        Rails.logger.warn(
          "profile_images:copy skipped #{record.class.name}##{record.id}: " \
          "missing or empty CarrierWave file (#{identifier})",
        )
        return :skipped
      end

      filename = File.basename(identifier.to_s).presence || "profile_image"
      content_type = file.content_type.presence
      blob = upload_blob(file, uploader, filename: filename, content_type: content_type)
      return :skipped unless blob

      attach_and_refresh_caches(record, blob)
      :copied
    rescue AlreadyAttachedError, ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      purge_orphan_blob(blob)
      :skipped
    rescue StandardError => e
      purge_orphan_blob(blob)
      Rails.logger.error(
        "profile_images:copy failed for #{record.class.name}##{record.id}: #{e.class}: #{e.message}",
      )
      :failed
    end

    def attachment_exists?(record)
      ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(
        record_type: record.class.name,
        record_id: record.id,
        name: "profile_image",
      )
    end

    def upload_blob(file, uploader, filename:, content_type:)
      if file.is_a?(CarrierWave::SanitizedFile) && file.path.present? && File.exist?(file.path)
        File.open(file.path, "rb") do |io|
          ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
            io: io,
            filename: filename,
            content_type: content_type,
            identify: true,
          )
        end
      else
        bytes = uploader.read
        return if bytes.blank?

        ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
          io: StringIO.new(bytes.b),
          filename: filename,
          content_type: content_type,
          identify: true,
        )
      end
    end

    def attach_and_refresh_caches(record, blob)
      ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
        record.lock!
        raise AlreadyAttachedError if attachment_exists?(record)

        ActiveStorage::Attachment.create!(
          name: "profile_image",
          record: record,
          blob: blob,
        )
        refresh_cached_articles!(record)
      end
    end

    def refresh_cached_articles!(record)
      record.association(:profile_image_attachment).reset
      cached_entity = Articles::CachedEntity.from_object(record)

      case record
      when User
        Article.where(user_id: record.id).update_all(cached_user: cached_entity)
      when Organization
        Article.where(organization_id: record.id).update_all(cached_organization: cached_entity)
      end
    end

    def purge_orphan_blob(blob)
      return unless blob&.persisted?
      return if ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(blob_id: blob.id)

      blob.purge
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn("profile_images:copy failed to purge orphan blob #{blob&.id}: #{e.message}")
    end
  end
end

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing the Profile Image Migration**

Okay, deep breath. Let's really dissect this, because messing up user profile images is a *huge* no-go. We're in production, and this migration needs to be flawless.

First, let's recap where we are. We've already got Active Storage enabled. Tables are created, routes are secured, and the `ProfileImageable` concern is in place. That's a solid foundation. This concern handles the `has_one_attached :profile_image`, dual-reads (Active Storage if present, CarrierWave fallback), and validation logic. We have upload and validation methods, checking file size, type, dimensions, and even stripping EXIF data. Crucially, there's a `profile_images:copy` rake task and `Images::CopyProfileImagesToActiveStorage` class that were presumably executed.

Now, we're being told that this deploy needs to *retire* CarrierWave for profile images on users and organizations, so all the previous images should be Active Storage and completely remove Carrierwave. However, we cannot break any existing images.

Okay, so what are the immediate red flags?

1.  **Column Dropping:** The prompt suggests removing CarrierWave entirely. That makes me start thinking about dropping the `profile_image` columns from the `users` and `organizations` tables. *But,* we absolutely cannot risk downtime or errors. Rails migrations in production, especially involving column removal, are notoriously tricky. If the app servers are still referencing the `profile_image` column and we drop it too early, we're looking at a crash.

2.  **Data Integrity:** The biggest question is, *what's the state of the data*? Has *every single* profile image been successfully migrated by `profile_images:copy`? This is the core risk we must understand to make any change. Are there still records using the `profile_image` column? Are there default images or external URLs stored in that column? What does `DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE` actually represent?

3.  **Code Dependencies:** We need to know what parts of the system still touch those legacy columns and how. The use of the `profile_image` column in `User`, `Organization`, `ProfileImageable`, `Articles::CachedEntity`, `ProfileImageUploader`, or even elsewhere has a high potential to be used. I am going to have to do a full code search. I need to know the potential for bugs if old data still exists and the database design does not account for this.

So, the immediate next steps? A thorough codebase search for `profile_image`, `DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE`, `Images::Profile`, and `CachedEntity` to understand the code that touches these values, and a *deep dive* into the data to verify that *every* legacy image has been migrated. This will determine how we safely remove CarrierWave entirely, without impacting anyone.

First, I'm going to look at the core image handling services. I'm expecting to find the nuts and bolts of image retrieval, security considerations around remote URLs, image creation, and probably some image optimization or resizing logic in there. I'll pay close attention to the interfaces and how these services interact with each other.

Next, I'll need to understand how these images are used within the application's broader context, so I need to check how the application deals with user banning, user updates, and mascot account creation - and how that impacts images, so I'll be looking at `app/services/moderator/banish_user.rb`, `app/services/users/update.rb`, and `app/services/users/create_mascot_account.rb`. I'll be looking for image handling logic within those files, and what actions are taken with images when a user is modified.

Then, I'll move into the controllers and concerns. The `app/controllers/concerns/image_uploads.rb` is screaming "image upload logic" and is likely where the image uploads are coordinated with the image services, so this is essential. I'll also be examining the `app/controllers/organizations_controller.rb` and `app/controllers/organization_settings_controller.rb` as these are probably the touch points for organizations needing to manage their profile images. I'll need to look at lines 260-300 and 110-145 in these files respectively. I'll also glance at `app/controllers/concerns/api/profile_images_controller.rb` to examine the API entry points.

Finally, the models! The `app/models/user.rb` and `app/models/organization.rb` are crucial. I'll be looking specifically around the `profile_image` attributes, ransackable attributes if they're used for searching, and any callbacks that might be manipulating the image data or associated records. I'm expecting to see validations related to image size, format, or perhaps some kind of image processing triggered on save or update. I need to understand the data model and how it relates to the image data.

With this list, I should be able to form a clear picture of how profile images are managed, stored, and used in this application. Let's dig in.

  module Profile
    # A convenience module for wrapping the Profile::Images logic.
    #
    # @param attribute [Symbol] named attribute that is an image_url
    #
    # @return [Module] for inclusion into the given class
    #
    # @example
    #   class User
    #     include Images::Profile.for(:image_url)
    #   end
    def self.for(attribute)
      Module.new do
        define_method("#{attribute}_for") do |length:|
          Images::Profile.call(public_send(attribute), length: length)
        end
      end
    end
    BACKUP_LINK = "https://thepracticaldev.s3.amazonaws.com/i/99mvlsfu5tfj9m7ku25d.png".freeze

    def self.call(image_url, length: 120)
      Optimizer.call(
        image_url || BACKUP_LINK,
        width: length,
        height: length,
        crop: "crop",
        never_imagga: true,
      )
    end
  end
end
=== safe_remote_profile_image_url.rb ===
module Images
  module SafeRemoteProfileImageUrl
    # Basic check for nil and blank URLs, alongside likely incomplete URLs, such as just "image.jpg".
    def self.call(url)
      if url&.start_with?("http")
        url.sub!("http://", "https://")
        url
      else
        Images::ProfileImageGenerator.call
      end
    end
  end
end

# Helpers included in ApplicationController for working with image files
module ImageUploads
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MAX_FILENAME_LENGTH = 250

  def long_filename?(image)
    image&.original_filename && image.original_filename.length > MAX_FILENAME_LENGTH
  end

  def file?(image)
    image.respond_to?(:original_filename)
  end

  def filename_too_long_message
    I18n.t("concerns.image_uploads.too_long", max: MAX_FILENAME_LENGTH)
  end

  def is_not_file_message # rubocop:disable Naming/PredicateName
    I18n.t("concerns.image_uploads.is_not_file")
  end
end

module Moderator
  class BanishUser < ManageActivityAndRoles
    DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE =
      "https://thepracticaldev.s3.amazonaws.com/i/99mvlsfu5tfj9m7ku25d.png".freeze

    attr_reader :user, :admin

    def self.call(admin:, user:)
      new(user: user, admin: admin).banish
    end

    def initialize(admin:, user:)
      super(user: user, admin: admin, user_params: {})
    end

    def banish
      BanishedUser.create(username: user.username, banished_by: admin)
      user.remove_from_mailchimp_newsletters if user.email?
      remove_profile_info
      # The role grant inside handle_user_status would emit user_suspended;
      # suppress it so banish reaches Core as a single user_banished event
      # (the two would race through the CDP and could downgrade Core's
      # moderation marker after the banish was already applied).
      User.skip_trackable_events do
        handle_user_status("Suspended", I18n.t("services.moderator.banish_user.spam_account"))
      end
      delete_organization
      delete_user_activity
      delete_comments
      delete_articles
      delete_user_podcasts
      reassign_and_bust_username
      delete_vomit_reactions
      # Banish destroys the account's content and identity, so Core treats it
      # like spam (prunes the Customer.io profile). The pre-banish username
      # rides along because trackable_payload now carries the spam_ rename.
      user.track!("user_banished", { "old_username" => user.old_username })
    end

    private

    def reassign_and_bust_username
      new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      if User.find_by(name: new_name) || User.find_by(username: new_username)
        new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
        new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      end
      user.update_columns(name: new_name, username: new_username, old_username: user.username,
                          profile_updated_at: Time.current)
      EdgeCache::Bust.call("/#{user.old_username}")
    end

    def remove_profile_info
      user.profile.clear!
      user.profile_image.purge if user.profile_image.attached?
      user.update_columns(profile_image: nil)
    end

    def delete_vomit_reactions
      Reaction.where(reactable: user, category: "vomit").delete_all
    end

    def delete_organization
      user.organizations.each do |organization|
        organization.destroy! if organization.users.count == 1
      end
    end
  end

      errors.append(is_not_file_message)
      false
    end

    def valid_filename?(image)
      return true unless long_filename?(image)

      errors.append(filename_too_long_message)
      false
    end

    def update_profile
      # We don't update `data` directly. This uses the store_accessors instead.
      @profile.assign_attributes(@updated_profile_attributes)

      @profile.data.slice!(*Profile.attributes)

      return unless resave_articles? && !@user.spam_or_suspended?

      @updated_user_attributes.any_key?(user_fields) ||

module Moderator
  class BanishUser < ManageActivityAndRoles
    DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE =
      "https://thepracticaldev.s3.amazonaws.com/i/99mvlsfu5tfj9m7ku25d.png".freeze

    attr_reader :user, :admin

    def self.call(admin:, user:)
      new(user: user, admin: admin).banish
    end

    def initialize(admin:, user:)
      super(user: user, admin: admin, user_params: {})
    end

    def banish
      BanishedUser.create(username: user.username, banished_by: admin)
      user.remove_from_mailchimp_newsletters if user.email?
      remove_profile_info
      # The role grant inside handle_user_status would emit user_suspended;
      # suppress it so banish reaches Core as a single user_banished event
      # (the two would race through the CDP and could downgrade Core's
      # moderation marker after the banish was already applied).
      User.skip_trackable_events do
        handle_user_status("Suspended", I18n.t("services.moderator.banish_user.spam_account"))
      end
      delete_organization
      delete_user_activity
      delete_comments
      delete_articles
      delete_user_podcasts
      reassign_and_bust_username
      delete_vomit_reactions
      # Banish destroys the account's content and identity, so Core treats it
      # like spam (prunes the Customer.io profile). The pre-banish username
      # rides along because trackable_payload now carries the spam_ rename.
      user.track!("user_banished", { "old_username" => user.old_username })
    end

    private

    def reassign_and_bust_username
      new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      if User.find_by(name: new_name) || User.find_by(username: new_username)
        new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
        new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      end
      user.update_columns(name: new_name, username: new_username, old_username: user.username,
                          profile_updated_at: Time.current)
      EdgeCache::Bust.call("/#{user.old_username}")
    end

    def remove_profile_info
      user.profile.clear!
      user.profile_image.purge if user.profile_image.attached?
      user.update_columns(profile_image: nil)
    end

    def delete_vomit_reactions
      Reaction.where(reactable: user, category: "vomit").delete_all
    end

    def delete_organization
      user.organizations.each do |organization|
        organization.destroy! if organization.users.count == 1
      end
    end
  end
end

require "mini_magick"

# Carrierwave uses MiniMagick for image processing. To prevent server timeouts
# we are setting the MiniMagick timeout lower.
MiniMagick.configure do |config|
  config.timeout = 10
end

module CarrierWaveInitializer
  def self.local_storage_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :file
      config.enable_processing = !Rails.env.test? # disabled for test
      config.asset_host = if Rails.env.production?
                            "https://#{ApplicationConfig['APP_DOMAIN']}"
                          end
    end
  end

  def self.standard_production_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :fog
      config.fog_directory = ApplicationConfig["AWS_BUCKET_NAME"]
      config.fog_attributes = { cache_control: "public, max-age=#{365.days.to_i}" }
      config.fog_credentials = {
        provider: "AWS",
        aws_access_key_id: ApplicationConfig["AWS_ID"],
        aws_secret_access_key: ApplicationConfig["AWS_SECRET"],
        region: ApplicationConfig["AWS_UPLOAD_REGION"].presence || ApplicationConfig["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"]
      }
    end
  end

  def self.forem_cloud_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :fog
      config.fog_directory = ApplicationConfig["AWS_BUCKET_NAME"]
      config.asset_host = "https://#{ApplicationConfig['APP_DOMAIN']}/remoteimages"
      config.fog_public = false
      config.fog_credentials = {
        provider: "AWS",
        use_iam_profile: true,
        region: "us-east-2"
      }
    end
  end

  def self.initialize!
    if Rails.env.production? && ENV["FILE_STORAGE_LOCATION"] != "file"
      if ENV["FOREM_CONTEXT"] == "forem_cloud"
        forem_cloud_config
      elsif ApplicationConfig["AWS_ID"].present?
        standard_production_config
      else
        local_storage_config
      end
    else
      local_storage_config
    end
  end
end

require "mini_magick"

# Carrierwave uses MiniMagick for image processing. To prevent server timeouts
# we are setting the MiniMagick timeout lower.
MiniMagick.configure do |config|
  config.timeout = 10
end

module CarrierWaveInitializer
  def self.local_storage_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :file
      config.enable_processing = !Rails.env.test? # disabled for test
      config.asset_host = if Rails.env.production?
                            "https://#{ApplicationConfig['APP_DOMAIN']}"
                          end
    end
  end

  def self.standard_production_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :fog
      config.fog_directory = ApplicationConfig["AWS_BUCKET_NAME"]
      config.fog_attributes = { cache_control: "public, max-age=#{365.days.to_i}" }
      config.fog_credentials = {
        provider: "AWS",
        aws_access_key_id: ApplicationConfig["AWS_ID"],
        aws_secret_access_key: ApplicationConfig["AWS_SECRET"],
        region: ApplicationConfig["AWS_UPLOAD_REGION"].presence || ApplicationConfig["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"]
      }
    end
  end

  def self.forem_cloud_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :fog
      config.fog_directory = ApplicationConfig["AWS_BUCKET_NAME"]
      config.asset_host = "https://#{ApplicationConfig['APP_DOMAIN']}/remoteimages"
      config.fog_public = false
      config.fog_credentials = {
        provider: "AWS",
        use_iam_profile: true,
        region: "us-east-2"
      }
    end
  end

  def self.initialize!
    if Rails.env.production? && ENV["FILE_STORAGE_LOCATION"] != "file"
      if ENV["FOREM_CONTEXT"] == "forem_cloud"
        forem_cloud_config
      elsif ApplicationConfig["AWS_ID"].present?
        standard_production_config
      else
        local_storage_config
      end
    else
      local_storage_config
    end
  end
end

Rails.application.reloader.to_prepare do
  CarrierWaveInitializer.initialize!
end

    before_action :set_cache_control_headers, only: :index

    def index
      @tag = Tag.find_by(name: params[:tag].downcase) || not_found

      if @tag.alias_for.present?
        redirect_permanently_to("/t/#{@tag.alias_for}")
        return
      end

      @page = (params[:page] || 1).to_i

      if user_signed_in?
        @moderators = User.with_role(:tag_moderator, @tag)
          .order(badge_achievements_count: :desc)
          .select(:username, :profile_image, :id)
      end

      set_number_of_articles(tag: @tag)

      set_stories(number_of_articles: @number_of_articles, tag: @tag, page: @page)

      set_surrogate_key_header @stories.map(&:record_key), @tag.record_key
      set_cache_control_headers(86400,
                                stale_while_revalidate: 1000,
                                stale_if_error: 86_400)
    end

      @num_published_articles = if tag.requires_approval?

                                else
                                  Rails.cache.fetch("#{tag.cache_key}/article-cached-tagged-count",

    # @param page [Integer] the page in the pagination
    # @param per_page [Integer] how many items do we return in our pagination result set

    # @return [Hash<Symbol,Object>] with keys :items and :total.

    def self.search_documents(user, term: nil, statuses: [], tags: [], page: 0, per_page: DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, subforem_id: nil)

  module Providers
    # Apple authentication provider, uses omniauth-apple as backend
    class Apple < Provider
      OFFICIAL_NAME = "Apple".freeze
      SETTINGS_URL = "https://appleid.apple.com/account/manage".freeze
      TRUSTED_CALLBACK_ORIGIN = "https://appleid.apple.com".freeze
      CALLBACK_PATH = "/users/auth/apple/callback".freeze

      def self.official_name
        OFFICIAL_NAME
      end

      def self.settings_url
        SETTINGS_URL
      end

      def self.sign_in_path(**kwargs)
        ::Authentication::Paths.sign_in_path(
          provider_name,
          **kwargs,
        )
      end

      def new_user_data
        # Apple sends `first_name` and `last_name` as separate fields
        # If both are omitted (e.g. subsequent logins or Hide My Email), we fall back to user_nickname to prevent Name Can't Be Blank exceptions
        name = I18n.t("services.authentication.providers.apple.name", first: info.first_name, last: info.last_name).strip
        name = name.presence || user_nickname

        user_data = {
          email: info.email,
          apple_username: user_nickname,
          name: name
        }

        user_data[:profile_image] = if Rails.env.test?
                                      Settings::General.mascot_image_url
                                    else
                                      Images::ProfileImageGenerator.call
                                    end

        user_data
      end

      def existing_user_data
        # Apple by default will send nil `first_name` and `last_name` after
        # the first login. To cover the case where a user disconnects their
        # Apple authorization, signs in again and then changes their name,
        # we update the username only if the name is not nil
        apple_username = info.first_name&.downcase
        return {} unless apple_username

        { apple_username: apple_username }
      end

      # For Apple we override this method because the `info` payload doesn't
      # include `nickname`. On top of not having a username, Apple allows users
      # to 'choose' the first_name & last_name sent our way so they are
      # definitely not assured to be unique. We still need `user_nickname` to
      # always be the same on each login so we use the email hash as suffix to
      # avoid collisions with other registrations with the same first_name
      def user_nickname
        if info.first_name.present? || info.last_name.present?
          # We sometimes get `info.first_name` and `info.last_name`
          [
            info.first_name&.downcase,
            info.last_name&.downcase,
            Digest::SHA512.hexdigest(info.email),
          ].join("_")[0...25]
        else
          # This covers an edge case where the Apple Id has already given
          # permissions to the forem auth and we don't have anything else
          # to work with other than the email
          ["user", Digest::SHA512.hexdigest(info.email)].join("_")[0...15]
        end
      end

      protected

      def cleanup_payload(auth_payload)
        auth_payload
      end
    end
  end
end

**Analyzing the Active Storage Migration: A Deep Dive**

Okay, let's break this down. We're moving profile pictures to Active Storage, but other uploads stay on CarrierWave. The critical constraint is: *no broken profile pictures in production*. The sentence "Take CarrierWave off the profile pictures of users and organizations" is key, but let's carefully consider exactly what this entails. We need to dissect EVERYTHING!

First, let's address the *`ProfileImageable`* concern.  Currently, it's a dual-read setup with Active Storage and CarrierWave. It leverages `ProfileImageUploader` for:
1.  **Legacy Read:** `legacy_profile_image_present?`, `legacy_profile_image_identifier`, etc., which are a clear nod to the old CarrierWave setup and fallbacks.
2.  **Remote Download:**  `download_and_attach_remote_profile_image` which uses CarrierWave's downloader, even when Active Storage is supposed to be managing the image.
3.  **Shared Constants:** It references constants from `ProfileImageUploader` (`MAX_FILE_SIZE`, `EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST`, etc.).
    *   Also, we have to look at the *tests*, which are allowing `ProfileImageUploader` to receive the `download!` message (e.g., in registrations, authentication, and user update specs) and `stub_const` for the max file size.

It's clear that Deploy 1 (which we're already working *with*) has `ProfileImageUploader` as a crutch, reading old CarrierWave images, downloading remote images, and sharing constants.  *But* the `ProfileImageUploader` itself is *also* used by `Tag`, `Page`, `Tweet`, `Podcast`, and `PodcastEpisode`! Therefore, *`ProfileImageUploader` stays*.  The tests, also, should *stay* so that we can verify that the functionality of the other models are still intact.

Now, consider *what happens to Users and Organizations*. This is where the crucial question arises.

How do we deal with legacy filenames or URLs in the *`users.profile_image`* and *`organizations.profile_image`* columns? We must revisit the prompt and understand the implications of "No deploy may break a profile picture anyone can see today. The old profile picture uploads are retired with this deploy. Take CarrierWave off the profile pictures of users and organizations."

Before Deploy 1 (our original state), profile pictures were *only* on CarrierWave. Deploy 1 added Active Storage and dual-read functionality. Now we have to think about what's *between* Deploy 1 and *this* deploy.

The key questions:

*(A) Should the DB columns `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image` be dropped, ignored, or kept in this deploy?*
*(B) Should `ProfileImageable` remove `legacy_profile_image_*` (CarrierWave fallback)?*
*(C) Should `Images::CopyProfileImagesToActiveStorage` / `lib/tasks/profile_images.rake` be kept or removed?*
*(D) What about `ProfileImageable` referencing `ProfileImageUploader`, `CarrierWave::Downloader::Base`, `BaseUploader`?*
*(E) What about `User` and `Organization` queries doing `.select(:id, :profile_image)`?*
*(F) What about `Moderator::BanishUser` (`user.update_columns(profile_image: nil)`)?*
*(G) What about `Article#cached_user` / `Article#cached_organization` and `ATTRIBUTES_CACHED_FOR_RELATED_ENTITY`?*
*(H) What about `User.ransackable_attributes`?*

Let's begin with (A) and the *database columns*.

We *CANNOT* drop those columns in the same deploy that *stops referencing* them, or while processes still have them in their ActiveRecord schema cache, or are still `SELECT profile_image`. Any action to that effect will result in a production crash.  If we remove the reference in code, and then run the migration, old processes will break. Even if `ignored_columns` is implemented, the migration must be delayed to the *next* deploy!

Back to the prompt: It's *ambiguous*. It does *NOT* say "drop the `profile_image` column."  Is "Take CarrierWave off the profile pictures of users and organizations" *also* about removing the CarrierWave fallback and dependency (even if we keep the column), or about ignoring, or *actually* dropping? Given the emphasis on zero-downtime and avoiding broken images, we need to think

require 'open-uri'
require 'ssrf_filter'
require 'addressable'
require 'carrierwave/downloader/remote_file'

module CarrierWave
  module Downloader
    class Base
      include CarrierWave::Utilities::Uri

      attr_reader :uploader

      def initialize(uploader)
        @uploader = uploader
      end

      ##
      # Downloads a file from given URL and returns a RemoteFile.
      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [url (String)] The URL where the remote file is stored
      # [remote_headers (Hash)] Request headers
      #
      def download(url, remote_headers = {})
        @current_download_retry_count = 0
        headers = remote_headers.
          reverse_merge('User-Agent' => "CarrierWave/#{CarrierWave::VERSION}")
        uri = process_uri(url.to_s)
        begin
          if skip_ssrf_protection?(uri)
            response = OpenURI.open_uri(process_uri(url.to_s), headers)
          else
            request = nil
            if ::SsrfFilter::VERSION.to_f < 1.1
              response = SsrfFilter.get(uri, headers: headers) do |req|
                request = req
              end
            else
              response = SsrfFilter.get(uri, headers: headers, request_proc: ->(req) { request = req }) do |res|
                res.body # ensure to read body
              end
            end
            response.uri = request.uri
            response.value
          end
        rescue StandardError => e
          if @current_download_retry_count < @uploader.download_retry_count
            @current_download_retry_count += 1
            sleep @uploader.download_retry_wait_time
            retry
          else
            raise CarrierWave::DownloadError, "could not download file: #{e.message}"
          end
        end
        CarrierWave::Downloader::RemoteFile.new(response)
      end

      ##
      # Processes the given URL by parsing it, and escaping if necessary. Public to allow overriding.
      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [url (String)] The URL where the remote file is stored
      #
      def process_uri(source)
        uri = Addressable::URI.parse(source)
        uri.host = uri.normalized_host
        # Perform decode first, as the path is likely to be already encoded
        uri.path = encode_path(decode_uri(uri.path)) if uri.path =~ CarrierWave::Utilities::Uri::PATH_UNSAFE
        uri.query = encode_non_ascii(uri.query) if uri.query
        uri.fragment = encode_non_ascii(uri.fragment) if uri.fragment
        URI.parse(uri.to_s)
      rescue URI::InvalidURIError, Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError
        raise CarrierWave::DownloadError, "couldn't parse URL: #{source}"
      end

      ##
      # If this returns true, SSRF protection will be bypassed.
      # You can override this if you want to allow accessing specific local URIs that are not SSRF exploitable.
      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [uri (URI)] The URI where the remote file is stored
      #
      # === Examples

      #

      #
      def skip_ssrf_protection?(uri)
        @uploader.skip_ssrf_protection
      end
    end

require 'open-uri'
require 'ssrf_filter'
require 'addressable'
require 'carrierwave/downloader/remote_file'

module CarrierWave
  module Downloader
    class Base
      include CarrierWave::Utilities::Uri

      attr_reader :uploader

      def initialize(uploader)
        @uploader = uploader
      end

      ##
      # Downloads a file from given URL and returns a RemoteFile.
      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [url (String)] The URL where the remote file is stored
      # [remote_headers (Hash)] Request headers
      #
      def download(url, remote_headers = {})
        @current_download_retry_count = 0
        headers = remote_headers.
          reverse_merge('User-Agent' => "CarrierWave/#{CarrierWave::VERSION}")
        uri = process_uri(url.to_s)
        begin
          if skip_ssrf_protection?(uri)
            response = OpenURI.open_uri(process_uri(url.to_s), headers)
          else
            request = nil
            if ::SsrfFilter::VERSION.to_f < 1.1
              response = SsrfFilter.get(uri, headers: headers) do |req|
                request = req
              end
            else
              response = SsrfFilter.get(uri, headers: headers, request_proc: ->(req) { request = req }) do |res|
                res.body # ensure to read body
              end
            end
            response.uri = request.uri
            response.value
          end
        rescue StandardError => e
          if @current_download_retry_count < @uploader.download_retry_count
            @current_download_retry_count += 1
            sleep @uploader.download_retry_wait_time
            retry
          else
            raise CarrierWave::DownloadError, "could not download file: #{e.message}"
          end
        end
        CarrierWave::Downloader::RemoteFile.new(response)
      end

      ##
      # Processes the given URL by parsing it, and escaping if necessary. Public to allow overriding.
      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [url (String)] The URL where the remote file is stored
      #
      def process_uri(source)
        uri = Addressable::URI.parse(source)
        uri.host = uri.normalized_host
        # Perform decode first, as the path is likely to be already encoded
        uri.path = encode_path(decode_uri(uri.path)) if uri.path =~ CarrierWave::Utilities::Uri::PATH_UNSAFE
        uri.query = encode_non_ascii(uri.query) if uri.query
        uri.fragment = encode_non_ascii(uri.fragment) if uri.fragment
        URI.parse(uri.to_s)
      rescue URI::InvalidURIError, Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError
        raise CarrierWave::DownloadError, "couldn't parse URL: #{source}"
      end

      ##
      # If this returns true, SSRF protection will be bypassed.
      # You can override this if you want to allow accessing specific local URIs that are not SSRF exploitable.
      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [uri (URI)] The URI where the remote file is stored
      #
      # === Examples
      #
      #     class CarrierWave::Downloader::CustomDownloader < CarrierWave::Downloader::Base
      #       def skip_ssrf_protection?(uri)
      #         uri.hostname == 'localhost' && uri.port == 80
      #       end
      #     end
      #
      #     my_uploader.downloader = CarrierWave::Downloader::CustomDownloader
      #
      def skip_ssrf_protection?(uri)
        @uploader.skip_ssrf_protection
      end
    end
  end
end

**Analyzing Remote Image Downloads and SSRF Vulnerabilities**

Okay, this is clean. I see that `ssrf_filter` is a dependency of `carrierwave`, which means it's already in the `Gemfile.lock`. Alternatively, we could directly use `SsrfFilter` itself, or consider `HTTParty`, `Net::HTTP`, or even `OpenURI`. The key here is that `SsrfFilter` *provides* SSRF protection for user-supplied URLs. Think of URLs like the one used by `api/v1/organizations`, or even for remote profile images, like `remote_profile_image_url = Images::SafeRemoteProfileImageUrl.call(image)`, and also for OAuth URLs.

Let me take a look at how we're testing this functionality in `spec/models/concerns/profile_imageable_spec.rb`, particularly how `remote_profile_image_url=` is tested. Ah, `WebMock` is stubbing the requests! It's using `stub_request(:get, url)` to simulate the download of a remote image, and it's verifying both successful downloads and failure scenarios. It's great to see that we're validating both happy and sad paths.

Now, because all of these libraries — `Net::HTTP`, `HTTParty`, `OpenURI`, and `SsrfFilter` — ultimately go through `Net::HTTP`, `WebMock` is able to intercept them all. Perfect.

I remember now why we had that specific configuration in `spec/rails_helper.rb`:

# Disable SSRF protection for CarrierWave specs
# See: https://github.com/carrierwaveuploader/carrierwave/issues/2531
allow_any_instance_of(CarrierWave::Downloader::Base)
  .to receive(:skip_ssrf_protection?).and_return(true)

The reason is that in the tests, `SsrfFilter` was trying to do DNS resolution (`Resolv.getaddresses`) *before* `WebMock` even got a chance to run. If a test stubs a URL like `https://example.com/avatar.png` or `https://dummyimage.com/400x400.jpg` in an offline container, `SsrfFilter.get` would try to resolve the DNS and fail with a `SsrfFilter::Error` if DNS is disabled. That's a good reminder.

**Architectural Deep Dive: Retiring CarrierWave Profile Images**

Alright, let's break this down systematically. I see a critical opportunity here, and we need to be meticulous. Line 249 of `rails_helper.rb` with the stubbed empty body is a clue; it highlights potential issues with our approach. The fact that an empty CarrierWave response doesn't error is a vulnerability. We're moving profile pictures and, importantly, retiring the *old* system. Let's make sure we handle every aspect correctly.

Here's my analysis:

1.  **`ProfileImageable` Decoupling:** We're going *all in* on Active Storage for profile images. This means aggressively removing every bit of CarrierWave coupling in `ProfileImageable`.

    *   Goodbye to all the legacy methods: `legacy_profile_image_present?`, `legacy_profile_image_identifier`, `legacy_profile_image_for_validation?`, and so on. They are *gone*.
    *   In `profile_image_url`, we're making sure it only uses the Active Storage URL if the image is attached.
    *   Remove legacy fallbacks in `active_storage_profile_image_url`.
    *   `validates :profile_image, presence: true` should work as is, per the test in `spec/models/organization_spec.rb`, which we need to confirm is passing *before* our change.
    *   For the remote download, we're building our *own* Active Storage downloader. No more `CarrierWave::Downloader::Base` and `ProfileImageUploader` in this context. A clean Active Storage download method is essential. We need to handle invalid URLs, redirects, HTTP errors, empty bodies, and content-type extraction, with SSRF protection.
    *   SSRFilter - We must consider `SsrfFilter` in the context of our tests and in production. We may use a helper `skip_ssrf_protection?` or `ForemInstance.private_network_allowed?` and test our SSRF considerations within `ProfileImageable` and any relevant specs, and check for `ssrf` in `app/` and `spec/`.
    *   The constants? Forget them. `MAX_PROFILE_IMAGE_SIZE`, `ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_EXTENSIONS`, `MAX_PROFILE_IMAGE_FRAMES`, and `MAX_PROFILE_IMAGE_STRIP_FRAMES` get defined directly in `ProfileImageable`.
    *   `ProfileImageUploader.enable_processing` is out! We replace it with `ProfileImageable.process_images` (or equivalent), making sure it's configurable and that the EXIF tests reflect this change. We adjust the `users/update_spec.rb` test to reflect the new constant name.

2.  **`Images::CopyProfileImagesToActiveStorage` and Related Tasks:** THIS is critical. Do we keep this, or eliminate?

    *   The service *explicitly* relies on the CarrierWave column and `ProfileImageUploader`. It's the backfill tool.
    *   Once the old images are "retired," we do *not* want to use code that contains CarrierWave dependencies.
    *   Since the goal is to *remove* CarrierWave, keeping it in the codebase means the dependency is not removed.

    Conclusion: `app/services/images/copy_profile_images_to_active_storage.rb`, the rake task, and associated tests need to be *deleted*. Once the CarrierWave images are retired, this service is meaningless.

3.  **Database Column `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image`:** We need to know who is reading and writing to the old CarrierWave DB column.

    *   We need to carefully review every place in the code that touches these columns. This includes controllers, services, models, and anywhere else `profile_image` is used. Specifically, we have to audit API controllers to ensure the values are not accidentally exposed in API responses.
    *   After careful review of these files, we need to decide what to do with the `profile_image` column in our next deploy:
        *   We can remove the DB column in a *future* deploy.
        *   We can `ignored_columns` in the models and drop it at a later date.

module Api
  module V1
    class OrganizationsController < ApiController
      include Api::OrganizationsController
      before_action :find_organization, only: %i[users listings articles]
      before_action :authenticate!, only: %i[create update destroy]
      before_action :authorize_admin, only: %i[update]
      before_action :authorize_super_admin, only: %i[create destroy]
      after_action :verify_authorized, only: %i[create update destroy]

      INDEX_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION = %i[
        id name profile_image slug summary tag_line url
      ].freeze

      SHOW_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION = %i[
        id username name summary twitter_username github_username url
        location created_at profile_image slug tech_stack tag_line story
      ].freeze

      def index
        per_page = (params[:per_page] || 30).to_i
        num = [per_page, per_page_max].min
        page = params[:page] || 1

        organizations = Organization.select(INDEX_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION).page(page).per(num)

        render json: organizations
      end

      def show
        # This is less RESTful than having a show action that would always assume an id
        # unless given e.g. a query parameter specifying a different lookup key.
        # The by-username lookup is the current default behavior, this approach
        # keeps it intact. Conventionally, the lookup would default to id-based if we keep both.
        finder = Organization.select(SHOW_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION)
        @organization = finder.find_by(id: params[:id_or_slug]) || finder.find_by(slug: params[:id_or_slug])
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @organization

        render :show
      rescue ArgumentError => e
        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      def create
        organization = Organization.new params_for_create
        authorize organization
        if organization.save!
          render json: {
            id: organization.id,
            name: organization.name,
            profile_image: organization.profile_image_url,
            slug: organization.slug,
            summary: organization.summary,
            tag_line: organization.tag_line,
            url: organization.url
          }, status: :created
        else
          render json: { error: organization.errors_as_sentence, status: 422 }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end
      rescue ArgumentError => e
        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      def update
        set_organization
        @organization.assign_attributes(organization_params)
        if @organization.save
          render json: {
            id: @organization.id,
            name: @organization.name,
            profile_image: @organization.profile_image_url,
            slug: @organization.slug,
            summary: @organization.summary,
            tag_line: @organization.tag_line,
            url: @organization.url
          }
        else
          render json: { error: @organization.errors_as_sentence, status: 422 }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end
      rescue ArgumentError => e
        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      def destroy
        set_organization
        Organizations::DeleteWorker.perform_async(@organization.id, @user.id, false)

        render json: { message: "deletion scheduled for organization with ID #{@organization.id}", status: 200 }
      rescue ArgumentError => e
        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      private

      def authorize_admin
        authorize Organization, :access?, policy_class: InternalPolicy
      end

      def organization_params
        params.require(:organization).permit(:id, :name, :profile_image, :slug, :summary, :tag_line, :url)
      end

      # Accepts either an image file or a remote url for an image in the :profile_image attribute
      def params_for_create
        image = params.dig(:organization, :profile_image)

        # If the user has given a url for the profile image, place it where it should be handled
        if image.is_a? String
          permitted_params = organization_params.to_h
          permitted_params.delete(:profile_image)
          permitted_params[:remote_profile_image_url] = Images::SafeRemoteProfileImageUrl.call(image)
        end
        permitted_params
      end

      def set_organization
        @organization = Organization.find_by(id: params[:id])
        not_found unless @organization
        authorize @organization
      end
    end
  end
end

messages.thinking:
**A Deep Dive into Profile Image Serialization**

Okay, here's the situation as I see it. We've got a potential pitfall in how we're handling `profile_image` serialization, and it requires a thorough investigation. My initial thought process is this:

I see a direct correlation between the `UsersController#update`, the `profile_images_migration_spec.rb` and the `app/javascript/onboarding/components/actions.js`. Specifically, the JSON response in the `update` action includes the `profile_image.url` which is being consumed by the onboarding process. This works because of how our specs are set up. Also, the `Api::V1::OrganizationsController#index` action has a problem. The issue is if the `profile_image` column is effectively ignored, which can occur, due to being in `ignored_columns` in either `User` or `Organization` models.

The implications are serious. First, in `UsersController#update`, we’re rendering JSON based on the `@user.as_json` which, in turn, calls `@user.serializable_hash`. If `profile_image` is in the `ignored_columns`, the `super` call in the `serializable_hash` method will not include `profile_image` in the resulting hash. This means the `json.dig("user", "profile_image", "url")` will return `nil`, crashing the onboarding image upload in the javascript. Second, in `Api::V1::OrganizationsController#index` which uses `Organization.select(INDEX_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION)`, and `profile_image` is ignored, the render would not include the image unless handled. The `Organization.select(:profile_image)` would still emit SQL that includes `profile_image` when it doesn't need to.

Now, let's explore `ProfileImageable#serializable_hash`. It's crucial that we consider how the method interacts with options passed to `as_json` (e.g., `user.as_json(only: %i[id username])`). When we call `user.as_json(only: %i[id username])` the `profile_image` should *not* be included unless explicitly requested or not excluded. However, when we do a `user.as_json` call with no options, the `profile_image` was previously included.

Now, regarding the `Api::V1::OrganizationsController#index`, and the `Organization.select()` query, we need to decide how to handle it when serializing. We have several options. The simplest being to update `Api::V1::OrganizationsController#index` to render the exact JSON attributes, to include the profile image separately. However, a better solution is to modify the `serializable_hash(options = nil)` method.

Here's my proposed logic for `serializable_hash(options = nil)`:

1.  If `options` has `:only`, include `"profile_image"` *only* if `"profile_image"` is in the `:only` array.
2.  Else if `options` has `:except`, include `"profile_image"` unless `"profile_image"` is in the `:except` array.
3.  Else (no `:only` and no `:except`), we need to decide if we want to include the image if we are doing a select. What if `Organization.select(:id, :name, :slug, :summary, :tag_line, :url)` was used? The `attributes` only has those specified keys. If we do `serializable_hash`, we still need to serialize the image with no restriction on options.

Also, what was returned *before* the changes? Previously the image URL was returned in a similar format.

Therefore, the final proposed logic is to make the `serializable_hash` include `"profile_image" => { "url" => profile_image_url }` under the following conditions:

*   If `options` is nil or doesn't restrict away `"profile_image"`.
*   If `options&.key?(:only)` -> only if `"profile_image"` is in the only option.
*   If `options&.key?(:except)` -> unless `"profile_image"` is in the except option.
*   Otherwise include it as long as `hash.key?("profile_image")` OR `self.class.ignored_columns.include?("profile_image")`

To be certain, I will now search through the codebase for usages of `.as_json`, `.to_json`, and `render json:` that involve `User` or `Organization` models. This will allow us to check if any tests perform a `.select(...).

**Analyzing the Profile Image Transition: A Deep Dive**

Okay, so I've been meticulously examining the implications of transitioning profile images from CarrierWave to Active Storage, one deploy at a time. The current focus is on how to integrate the change without disrupting existing functionality in production, especially considering the need for zero downtime. The tests I've reviewed, like `user_decorator_spec.rb` and `organization_decorator_spec.rb`, highlight how the `as_json` method is currently employed, particularly the nuances of selectively including or excluding the `profile_image` key. The current `serializable_hash` method handles this gracefully, but the existing code relies heavily on the `profile_image` database column.

The crucial question is whether to simply ignore the `profile_image` column in the models or to drop the column in the database immediately. Considering the requirement for zero-downtime, and our Forem's architecture, I've concluded that the safer and more appropriate approach is to add `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]` to both `User` and `Organization` and remove all direct database column references. This allows us to transition the data gracefully while maintaining availability. This strategy ensures that while the old column remains in the database during the deploy, the application will no longer interact with it.

I've carefully scrutinized the entire codebase, meticulously checking every instance where `profile_image` is mentioned within the `User` and `Organization` models and associated services and controllers. I've noted a lot of places where column selection in SQL needs to be updated. For example, queries that select specific columns from the database, like `User.select(:id, :profile_image)`, must be updated to omit the database column. Some services, like `BanishUser`, will need to be refactored to eliminate calls to update columns that are no longer accessible. Other changes are straightforward removal from lists, like removing `profile_image` from the `SHOW_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION`, and other attributes lists. And then there are other cases, such as `ALLOWED_USER_PARAMS`, where `profile_image` needs to be retained because they are related to uploads. Finally, I've got to check usages of `ATTRIBUTES_CACHED_FOR_RELATED_ENTITY` and associated views to ensure they correctly reflect this change as well.

The rationale for this two-step approach is clear: in Rails, dropping a column during a deploy where it's still being queried by in-flight requests can lead to crashes. By adding the `ignored_columns` first and removing references, we ensure a clean transition, and then the column can be removed in a subsequent deploy, eliminating the risk of downtime.

  "output_head": "class OnboardingsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_user!
  before_action :check_suspended, only: %i[notifications]
  before_action :set_cache_control_headers, only: %i[show tags]
  before_action :set_no_cache_header, only: %i[update users_and_organizations]
  after_action :verify_authorized, only: %i[update checkbox]

  SUGGESTED_USER_ATTRIBUTES = %i[id name username summary profile_image].freeze
  TAG_ONBOARDING_ATTRIBUTES = %i[id name taggings_count].freeze
  ALLOWED_USER_PARAMS = %i[last_onboarding_page username name summary profile_image].freeze
  ALLOWED_CHECKBOX_PARAMS = %i[checked_code_of_conduct checked_terms_and_conditions].freeze
  ALLOWED_NOTIFICATION_PARAMS = %i[email_newsletter email_digest_periodic].freeze

  def show
    set_surrogate_key_header "onboarding-slideshow"
  end

  def users_and_organizations
    suggested_follows = suggested_user_follows + suggested_organization_follows
    @suggestions = ApplicationDecorator.decorate_collection(suggested_follows)
  end

  def tags
    @tags = Tags::SuggestedForOnboarding.call
      .select(TAG_ONBOARDING_ATTRIBUTES)

    render json: @tags
    set_surrogate_key_header Tag.table_key, @tags.map(&:record_key)
  end

  def update
    authorize User, :onboarding_update?

    user_params = {}

    if params[:user]
      if unset_username?
        return render json: { errors: I18n.t("users_controller.username_blank") }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      sanitize_user_params
      user_params = params[:user].permit(ALLOWED_USER_PARAMS)
    end

    update_result = Users::Update.call(current_user, user: user_params, profile: profile_params)

    if update_result.success?
      render json: {}, status: :ok
    else
      render json: { errors: update_result.errors_as_sentence }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def checkbox
    authorize User, :onboarding_checkbox_update?

    if params[:user]
      current_user.assign_attributes(params[:user].permit(ALLOWED_CHECKBOX_PARAMS))
    end

    current_user.saw_onboarding = true

    if current_user.save
      render json: {}, status: :ok
    else
      render json: { errors: errors }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def notifications
    authorize User, :onboarding_notifications_checkbox_update?

    if params[:notifications]
      current_user.notification_setting.assign_attributes(params[:notifications].permit(ALLOWED_NOTIFICATION_PARAMS))
    end

    current_user.saw_onboarding = true

    success = current_user.notification_setting.save
    notifications_updated_response(success, current_user.notification_setting.errors_as_sentence)
  end

  # DEV-specific custom actions for onboarding.
  # This path won't be used unless the feature flag is turned on.
  # The idea is that this could be a more custom endpoint later on, but now is just hardcoded.
  def custom_actions
    authorize User, :onboarding_update?
  
    if params[:follow_challenges]
      tag = Tag.find_by(name: "devchallenge")
      current_user.follow(tag) if tag
    end
  
    if params[:follow_education_tracks]
      tag = Tag.find_by(name: "deved")
      current_user.follow(tag) if tag
    end
  
    if params[:follow_featured_accounts]
      org = Organization.find_by_username("googleai")
      current_user.follow(org) if org
    end
  
    respond_to do |format|
      format.json { render json: {}, status: :ok }
    end
  end

  def newsletter
    respond_to do |format|
      format.json do
        rendered_content = render_to_string(partial: "onboardings/newsletter",
                                            formats: [:html],
                                            layout: false)
        render json: { content: rendered_content }
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def unset_username?
    params[:user].key?(:username) && params[:user][:username].blank?
  end

  def sanitize_user_params
    params[:user].compact_blank!
  end

  def profile_params
    params[:profile]&.permit(Profile.static_fields + Profile.attributes)
  end

  def notifications_updated_response(success, errors)
    status = success ? 200 : 422

    respond_to do |format|
      format.json { render json: { errors: errors }, status: status }
    end
  end

  def suggested_organization_follows
    Organizations::SuggestProminent.call(current_user)
  end

  def suggested_user_follows
    Users::SuggestProminent.call(current_user,
                                 attributes_to_select: SUGGESTED_USER_ATTRIBUTES)
  end
end

require "net/http"
require "ssrf_filter"

# Active Storage support for User and Organization profile pictures.
module ProfileImageable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MAX_PROFILE_IMAGE_SIZE = 8.megabytes
  ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = %w[jpg jpeg jpe gif png ico bmp dng webp].freeze
  ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[
    image/jpeg
    image/gif
    image/png
    image/x-icon
    image/vnd.microsoft.icon
    image/bmp
    image/x-ms-bmp
    image/webp
    image/x-adobe-dng
    image/tiff
  ].freeze
  MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION = 4096
  MAX_IMAGE_FRAMES = 500
  MAX_STRIP_FRAMES = 150
  MAX_REMOTE_DOWNLOAD_REDIRECTS = 5

  mattr_accessor :enable_processing, default: !Rails.env.test?

  included do
    self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]

    has_one_attached :profile_image

    before_save :record_profile_image_attachment_change
    before_save :strip_profile_image_exif
    after_commit :cleanup_profile_image_tempfiles
    after_rollback :cleanup_profile_image_tempfiles

    validate :validate_profile_image
  end

  attr_reader :remote_profile_image_url

  def profile_image=(attachable)
    @remote_profile_image_url = nil
    @profile_image_download_error = nil

    if attachable.nil? || attachable == ""
      super(nil)
    elsif attachable.is_a?(String)
      if (blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(attachable))
        super(blob)
      else
        # Ignore non-signed string assignments (e.g. URL strings passed directly)
        self
      end
    else
      super(attachable)
    end
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url=(url)
    @remote_profile_image_url = nil
    @profile_image_download_error = nil

    return if url.blank?

    unless url.is_a?(String)
      self.profile_image = url
      return
    end

    @remote_profile_image_url = url
    download_and_attach_remote_profile_image(url)
  end

  def profile_image_url
    active_storage_profile_image_url if profile_image.attached?
  end

  def serializable_hash(options = nil)
    super.tap do |hash|
      hash["profile_image"] = { "url" => profile_image_url } if include_profile_image_in_serialization?(options)
    end
  end

  private

  def include_profile_image_in_serialization?(options)
    return false unless options.nil? || options.is_a?(Hash)

    if options && options[:only].present?
      Array(options[:only]).map(&:to_s).include?("profile_image")
    elsif options && options[:except].present?
      Array(options[:except]).map(&:to_s).exclude?("profile_image")
    else
      true
    end
  end

  def active_storage_profile_image_url
    attachment = profile_image.attachment
    return unless attachment

    if attachment.blob&.persisted?
      format_active_storage_url(
        Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_blob_path(profile_image, only_path: true),
      )
    elsif persisted? && profile_image_attachment&.persisted?
      format_active_storage_url(
        Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_blob_path(profile_image_attachment, only_path: true),
      )
    elsif attachment.blob
      format_active_storage_url(
        "/rails/active_storage/blobs/#{attachment.blob.key}/#{attachment.blob.filename}",
      )
    end
  end

  def format_active_storage_url(path)
    return path unless Rails.env.production? && URL.domain.present?

    URL.url(path)
  end

  def record_profile_image_attachment_change
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = attachment_changes["profile_image"].present?
  end

  def profile_image_changed?
    @profile_image_attachment_changed == true
  end

  def download_and_attach_remote_profile_image(url)
    uri = parse_remote_profile_image_uri(url)
    response, final_uri = fetch_remote_profile_image(uri)
    body = response.body
    return if body.blank?

    content_type = response["content-type"]&.split(";")&.first&.strip
    filename = remote_profile_image_filename(final_uri)
    self.profile_image = {
      io: StringIO.new(body.b),
      filename: filename,
      content_type: content_type
    }
    @remote_profile_image_url = url
  rescue StandardError => e
    @profile_image_download_error = "could not download file: #{e.message}"
  end

  def parse_remote_profile_image_uri(url)
    parsed = Addressable::URI.parse(url.to_s)
    parsed.host = parsed.normalized_host if parsed.host.present?
    uri = URI.parse(parsed.to_s)
    raise ArgumentError, "invalid URL scheme" unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?

    uri
  end

  def fetch_remote_profile_image(uri)
    if Rails.env.test?
      fetch_remote_profile_image_without_ssrf(uri)
    else
      request = nil
      response = SsrfFilter.get(
        uri,
        headers: { "User-Agent" => "Forem" },
        request_proc: ->(req) { request = req },
      ) { |res| res.body }
      response.value
      [response, request&.uri || uri]
    end
  end

  def fetch_remote_profile_image_without_ssrf(uri)
    current_uri = uri
    (MAX_REMOTE_DOWNLOAD_REDIRECTS + 1).times do
      response = Net::HTTP.start(
        current_uri.host,
        current_uri.port,
        use_ssl: current_uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: 10,
        read_timeout: 10,
      ) do |http|
        request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(current_uri)
        request["User-Agent"] = "Forem"
        http.request(request)
      end

      if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPRedirection) && response["location"].present?
        current_uri = parse_remote_profile_image_uri(URI.join(current_uri.to_s, response["location"]).to_s)
        next
      end

      response.value
      return [response, current_uri]
    end

    raise "too many redirects"
  end

  def remote_profile_image_filename(uri)
    basename = File.basename(uri.path.to_s)
    return "profile_image" if basename.blank? || basename == "/"

    basename
  end

  def validate_profile_image
    if @profile_image_download_error.present?
      errors.add(:profile_image, @profile_image_download_error)
      return
    end

    change = attachment_changes["profile_image"]
    return unless change.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne)

    blob = change.blob
    validate_profile_image_size(blob)
    validate_profile_image_type(blob)
    validate_profile_image_dimensions_and_frames(change) if errors[:profile_image].empty?
  end

  def validate_profile_image_size(blob)
    max_size = MAX_PROFILE_IMAGE_SIZE
    if blob.byte_size > max_size
      errors.add(
        :profile_image,
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.max_size_error",
          max_size: ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(max_size),
        ),
      )
    elsif blob.byte_size < 1
      errors.add(
        :profile_image,
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.min_size_error",
          min_size: ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(1),
        ),
      )
    end
  end

  def validate_profile_image_type(blob)
    ext = blob.filename.extension&.downcase
    if ext.present? && ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_EXTENSIONS.exclude?(ext)
      errors.add(
        :profile_image,
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.extension_allowlist_error",
          extension: ext.inspect,
          allowed_types: ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_EXTENSIONS.join(", "),
        ),
      )
      return
    end

    return if ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(blob.content_type)

    errors.add(
      :profile_image,
      I18n.t(
        "errors.messages.content_type_allowlist_error",
        content_type: blob.content_type,
        allowed_types: ALLOWED_PROFILE_IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES.join(", "),
      ),
    )
  end

  def validate_profile_image_dimensions_and_frames(change)
    with_attachable_path(change) do |path, io|
      dimensions = FastImage.size(io || path)
      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)

      if dimensions && (dimensions[0] > MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION || dimensions[1] > MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION)
        errors.add(:profile_image, :invalid)
        return
      end

      if ProfileImageable.enable_processing &&
          %w[image/gif image/webp].include?(change.blob.content_type) &&
          path.present?
        begin
          if MiniMagick::Image.new(path).frames.count > MAX_IMAGE_FRAMES
            errors.add(
              :profile_image,
              I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.too_many_frames", frame_max: MAX_IMAGE_FRAMES),
            )
          end
        rescue Timeout::Error
          errors.add(:profile_image, I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.timeout"))
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def strip_profile_image_exif
    return unless ProfileImageable.enable_processing

    change = attachment_changes["profile_image"]
    return unless change.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne)
    return if change.blob.content_type&.include?("svg")

    with_attachable_path(change) do |source_path, _io|
      return if source_path.blank?

      image = MiniMagick::Image.open(source_path)
      image.auto_orient
      image.strip unless image.frames.count > MAX_STRIP_FRAMES

      ext = File.extname(change.blob.filename.to_s)
      output = Tempfile.new(["profile_image", ext])
      output.binmode
      image.write(output.path)
      output.rewind

      @profile_image_tempfiles ||= []
      @profile_image_tempfiles << output

      attachment_changes["profile_image"] = ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne.new(
        "profile_image",
        self,
        {
          io: output,
          filename: change.blob.filename.to_s,
          content_type: change.blob.content_type
        },
      )
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data: #{e}")
  end

  def with_attachable_path(change)
    attachable = change.attachable
    case attachable
    when ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile
      yield attachable.tempfile.path, attachable.tempfile
    when Rack::Test::UploadedFile, File, Tempfile
      yield attachable.path, attachable
    when Pathname
      File.open(attachable, "rb") { |f| yield attachable.to_s, f }
    when Hash
      io = attachable[:io] || attachable["io"]
      if io.respond_to?(:path) && io.path.present?
        yield io.path, io
      elsif io
        io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
        ext = File.extname(change.blob.filename.to_s)
        temp = Tempfile.new(["profile_image_check", ext])
        temp.binmode
        IO.copy_stream(io, temp)
        temp.flush
        io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
        begin
          yield temp.path, temp
        ensure
          temp.close!
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def cleanup_profile_image_tempfiles
    return unless @profile_image_tempfiles

    @profile_image_tempfiles.each do |file|
      file.close unless file.closed?
      file.unlink if file.respond_to?(:path) && file.path && File.exist?(file.path)
    rescue StandardError
      nil
    end
    @profile_image_tempfiles = nil
  end
end
